validity.recommendation: Verify Diameter — every independent source found gives 1420 mm ("Ду 1420"), none gives 1400 mm. Consider recording it the same way GEM already records the sibling trunk P0768 (Urengoy-Pomary-Uzhgorod), which carries a dual value '1420, 1400' (nominal/OD vs a derived ID figure) — the current single value 1400 mm looks like the same ID-vs-nominal artifact seen elsewhere in this system, not a fabricated number. Also verify StartYear1=1982: both independent sources that give a commissioning date say 1983, and Ukrainian Wikipedia's dedicated page on this exact corridor states construction ran 1980-1983 across parallel strings — 1982 could legitimately be the first-thread commissioning while 1983 is the corridor's completion, but that needs a source that actually says so; don't just move the year without one. Separately (worth a note for the cluster-adjudication pass, NOT a duplicate flag against P0789 itself): Ukrainian Wikipedia describes 'Urengoy-Novopskov' as TWO parallel 1420mm-throughout strings (nitky), collectively named as GEM records this one row, plus a THIRD, differently-configured string that changes diameter partway (1420mm Urengoy-to-Petrovsk, then ~1200mm Petrovsk-to-Novopskov) that it calls 'Urengoy-Petrovsk'. GEM's P0790 'Petrovsk-Novopskov Gas Pipeline' (609 km, 1220 mm) looks like it could be exactly that third string's downstream half — worth checking whether the upstream Urengoy-to-Petrovsk half of that third string is captured anywhere in the Ukraine scope, or whether GEM's separate (non-Ukraine) 'Urengoy-Petrovsk Gas Pipeline' wiki entity already covers it. This is an open question, not a resolved duplicate.
validity.researcher_notes: Checked every citation already on the gem.wiki page first. Two are dead: energybase.ru (https://energybase.ru/pipeline/urengoy-novopskov) now returns an IP-block notice, no content retrievable; ungg.ru (http://www.ungg.ru/.../135-urengoj-novopskov) 404s. tsoua.com/en/about-us/key-facts/ (used for the owner claim) 403s for both WebFetch and url_verifier. The remaining wiki-cited sources (radiosvoboda.org, vesti.ru, eadaily.com) are about Luhansk occupation / EU gas-purchase policy / Gazprom dismantling OTHER named compressor stations (Valuyki, Pervomayskaya, Dolzhanskaya on other lines) — none of them names or gives specs for Urengoy-Novopskov, so they don't corroborate the row's numeric values even though they're live. eegas.com (2009 Russia-Ukraine dispute piece) is likewise tangential. So the sheet's own citation list, on inspection, supports almost none of the actual data-point values. Went to independent search instead. ru.wikipedia's 'Газотранспортная система России' (already cite_note-9 on the wiki page, so it's a source the row itself already points to, but I verified it directly) states verbatim: 'Уренгой — Новопсков. Длина 3609 км. Диаметр труб – 1420 мм, давление газа – 75 атм. Введён в эксплуатацию в 1983 году.' — length matches GEM exactly (3609 km) but diameter (1420 vs GEM's 1400) and start year (1983 vs GEM's 1982) do not. Ukrainian Wikipedia's dedicated page 'Уренгой — Петровськ — Новопсков' independently corroborates 1420 mm and an overall 1980-1983 construction window, and explains the corridor as parallel strings (see recommendation). A currently-open repair tender (bicotender.ru/tender188701147.html, GAZSTROYPROMB/Gazprom Transgaz Yugorsk, Peregrebnenskoye LPUMG) for capital repair with pipe replacement on 'МГ «Уренгой-Новопсков» Ду 1420' at km 685-718 and km 718-734 independently confirms the pipe is still classed at Ду 1420 (not 1400) and is under active maintenance today (evidence for Status, not just diameter). uglevodorody.ru's reference entry lists Gazprom as owner/operator and status 'в эксплуатации' (dated 2020). No source I found states a length of anything other than 3609 km or (from mirrors that appear to trace to one origin, V.G. Chirskov's 'Минефтегазстрой СССР в лицах') a conflicting 3341 km for what may be a differently-scoped figure — flagging the alternate number for awareness but treating GEM's 3609 km as adequately corroborated by the one clean, independent, already-wiki-cited Wikipedia figure. No source found gives a capacity/throughput figure in bcm/y for this specific line, so Capacity=31 (bcm/y) remains genuinely unresolved — not fabricating a citation for it.

validity.recommendation: Directionally the Owner split (Gazprom PJSC + Gas Transmission System Operator of Ukraine, no percentages) is consistent with country-scope guidance — the Russian-territory portion is Gazprom's (independently supported: the bicotender.ru repair tender is contracted through 'ООО Газпром трансгаз Югорск', a Gazprom subsidiary, on the Russian section) and the Ukrainian portion should sit with the state GTS rather than Gazprom. But I could not independently re-verify the Ukrainian half: the row's own cited support for that half (tsoua.com key-facts page, a LinkedIn company page) 403s / isn't a citable public source, and I found no other public source specifically naming this line's Ukrainian-section owner. Worth a second look at whether the correct Ukrainian-side owner of record should be the asset-holding company 'Main Gas Pipelines of Ukraine' (MGU) with the Gas TSO of Ukraine recorded as operator rather than owner, and at adding ownership percentages once a working source is found.
validity.researcher_notes: No independent public source located that names this specific pipeline's Ukrainian-section owner/operator by entity name (TSOU vs MGU) with a verifiable, live URL. Not proposing a fill for Owner because I can't back it with a passing citation; flagging as a caveat instead of silently leaving it.

Existence is solid and multiply, independently corroborated: ru.wikipedia's GTS-Russia article, Ukrainian Wikipedia's dedicated corridor page, a live 2020s Gazprom-side capital-repair tender referencing exact km markers (685-718, 718-734) on 'МГ «Уренгой-Новопсков»', and a separate industry reference entry (uglevodorody.ru) — different origins, none tracing to GEM or to each other. Route (Urengoy, Yamalo-Nenets, Russia -> Novopskov, Luhansk Oblast, Ukraine) and classification (a Soviet-era 1420mm-class trunk transmission line, i.e. correctly 'transmission' not a gathering/feeder line) are both consistent across every source. Checked against the 39-pipeline roster for a duplicate: P0789 is NOT the same physical corridor as P0768 (Urengoy-Pomary-Uzhgorod, a different Russian-field-to-Slovak-border route via western Ukraine), P0774 (Progress, originates at Yamburg not Urengoy), P0790 (Petrovsk-Novopskov) or P0791 (Orenburg-Novopskov) — Novopskov is a real, well-documented convergence hub for several distinct Soviet-era trunklines from different Russian origin fields, matching the multi-string-trunk pattern already established elsewhere in this country pass; no hard duplicate found for P0789 itself (see the spec-concern entry above for an open, unresolved question about whether P0790 corresponds to part of a third parallel string of this same corridor family).

fills.researcher_notes: uglevodorody.ru's reference entry lists status 'в эксплуатации' (in operation); a live capital-repair tender for pipe replacement at km 685-718 and 718-734 on this exact line (contracted via Gazprom Transgaz Yugorsk / Peregrebnenskoye LPUMG) is independent, current evidence of an actively maintained, in-service line, not a defect indicating any change to Status.
Listed as a 'газопровод' (gas pipeline) in Russia's national gas-transport-system article and every other source consulted; unambiguous.

Consistently referred to as 'МГ' (магистральный газопровод = trunk/transmission gas pipeline), a 1420mm-class, 75 atm long-distance trunk built 1980-1983 — this is a transmission trunk, not a gathering/feeder/process line.
Both endpoints (Urengoy in Yamalo-Nenets AO, Russia; Novopskov in Luhansk Oblast, Ukraine) are named explicitly and consistently in both Wikipedia sources describing this exact corridor.

summary: P0789 (Urengoy-Novopskov) is real and correctly classified/routed, but the sheet's own citations are almost entirely dead or off-topic; independently, Length=3609km matches ru.wikipedia exactly, while Diameter=1400mm (every other source says 1420mm) and StartYear1=1982 (sources say 1983) are unresolved spec concerns, Capacity=31bcm/y and the Ukrainian-side Owner attribution remain UNRESOLVED (no independent source found), and a possible link between P0790 and a third parallel 'Urengoy-Petrovsk' string is flagged for the cluster pass, not resolved here.
